questions.q_en: A train running at the speed of 54 km/h crosses a platform in 45 seconds. If the platform is renovated and its length is double, then the same train crosses the platform in 65 seconds. Find the length of the train.
questions.solution_en:
Speed of the train = 54 * 5/18 = 15 m/sec [To convert km/h into m/sec multiply by 5/18]

Distance = Speed * Time

Let the length of the train and platform be x m and y m respectively.

x + y = 45 * 15 ... (i)

x + 2y = 65 * 15 ... (ii)

From (i) and (ii)

x = 375 m

questions.q_en: Two trains travel in opposite directions and cross each other in 18 seconds. If trains start moving in the same direction, then the faster train crosses the slower train in 90 seconds. The speed of the slower train is 144 km/h and the length of the faster train is 960 m, then find the speed of the faster train.
questions.solution_en:
Let the length of the slower train and the speed of the faster train be 'X' m and S km/h respectively.

Distance = Time * Speed

960 + Y = 18 * (S + 144) * 5/18 [To convert km/h into m/sec multiply by 5/18]

960 + Y = 5S + 720

Y = 5S - 240 ..... (i)

960 + Y = 90 * (S - 144) * 5/18

960 + Y = 25S - 3600

Y = 25S - 4560 ..... (ii)

From (i) and (ii),

5S - 240 = 25S - 4560

20S = 4320

S = 216 km/h

questions.q_en: A train of length 180 m passes a 320 m platform in 40 s, then meets and crosses an oncoming train of length L m moving at 54 km/h in 12 s. Find L.
questions.solution_en:
First train's speed = (180+320)/40 = 500/40 = 25/2 m/s

Opposing train speed = 54 * 5/18 = 15 m/s

Relative speed = 25/2 + 15 = 55/2 m/s

Crossing time = 12 s

Distance = (55/2) X 12 = 330 m

Hence, 180 + L = 330

L = 150 m

questions.q_en: A train passes a platform in 30 s and a signal post in 18 s, travelling at 72 km/h throughout. The platform is 120 m shorter than the train. Find the lengths of the train and the platform.
questions.solution_en:
Let L = train length (m)

Platform length = L − 120

Speed = 72 km/h = 72 X 5/18 = 20 m/s

Time to pass platform:

[L + (L − 120)]/20 = 30

=> 2L − 120 = 600

=> 2L = 720

=> L = 360 m

Platform = 360 − 120 = 240 m

questions.q_en: A train running at the speed of 72 km/h crosses a 240 m long platform in 18 seconds. How long will it take to cross a bridge which is 720 m long?
questions.solution_en:
Let length of train = L

Speed = 72 x 5/18 = 20 m/s

Distance covered to cross platform = L+240

(L+240)/20 = 18

=> L + 240 = 360

=> L = 120m

Time taken to cross bridge = (720+120)/20 = 840/20 = 42 s

questions.q_en: Train A of length 800 meters crosses another train B of length 1200 meters, running on a parallel track in the opposite direction in 25 seconds. If train B cross a pole in 1 minute 20 seconds, then what is the speed of train A?
questions.solution_en:
Speed of train B = 1200/80 = 15

Let speed of train A = a m/s

According to the question,

(1200 + 800)/(a + 15) = 25

=> a + 15 = 2000/25

=> a = 80 - 15 = 65 m/s

questions.q_en: Two trains start from stations A and B, 300 km apart, and travel towards each other at 60 km/h and 90 km/h. They cross and continue to the opposite stations. What is the difference in their arrival times at the opposite ends?
questions.solution_en:
Time taken to meet = 300/(60+90) = 2 h

First train covers (60 X 2 =) 120 km to meeting.

Remaining distance for first train to cover = 300−120 = 180 km

=> time taken = 180/60 = 3 h

=> total time taken = 5 h

Second train covers (90 X 2 =) 180 km to meeting.

Remaining distance for second train to cover = 300−180 = 120 km

=> time taken = 120/90 = 1.333 h = 1 h 20 min

=> total time taken = 3 h 20 min

Required difference = 5 h − 3 h 20 min = 1 h 40 min

questions.q_en: Trains A and B, length 200 m and 150 m respectively, on parallel tracks in opposite directions cross in 20 s. A then crosses a 400 m platform in 60 s. Find their speeds (km/h).
A train overtakes two persons who are walking at 4kmph and 8kmph in the same direction as the train is moving in 15 and 25 seconds respectively. Find the speed of the train.
questions.solution_en:
Speed of first man is 4kmph = 4*5/18 = 10/9 m/s

And second man is 8kmph = 8*5/18 = 20/9 m/s

Let the speed of the train be x m/s.

Then, the relative speed is (x - 10/9) m/s and (x - 20/9) m/s

Now, length of the train = relative speed*time taken to pass a man

So, (x-10/9)*15 = (x-20/9)*25

(9x-10)*15 = (9x-20)*25

135x - 150 = 225x - 500

90x = 350

x = 35/9 m/s

Hence, speed of the train = (35/9)*(18/5) = 14kmph

questions.q_en: Two trains P and Q start running from station X to station Y with the speed of 100 km/h and 80 km/h respectively. If train P starts 30 minutes later than train Q from station X and reaches station Y 30 minutes before train Q, then what is the distance between stations X and Y?
questions.solution_en:
Let the distance between stations X and Y = 'd' km

Time taken by train Q - time taken by train P = 30 + 30 = 60 minutes = 1 hour

d/80 - d/100 = 1

d/400 = 1

d = 400 km

questions.q_en: Train P crosses a pole in 30 seconds whereas train Q crosses the pole in 72 seconds. The lengths of train P and train Q are in the ratio of 3:5. Find the ratio of speeds of P and Q.
questions.solution_en:
Let, the length of train P = 3s m and

the length of train Q = 5s m

Speed of train P = 3s/30 m/s

Speed of train Q = 5s/72 m/s

Required ratio = (3/30) : (5/72) = 36 : 25

the length of train Q = 5s m

Speed of train P = 3s/30 m/s

Speed of train Q = 5s/72 m/s

questions.q_en: Two trains - A and B start from Patna and Asansol respectively towards each other at the same time and they meet after 8 hours. The speed of train A is 36 km/h less than the speed of train B and the distance between Patna and Asansol is 720 km. What is the speed of train A?
questions.solution_en:
Let speed of train A = x km/h and speed of train B = (x + 36) km/h

Relative speed = (2x + 36) km/h

According to the question,

720/(2x + 36) = 8

=> x = 27 km/h

questions.q_en: Pawan Express is a 300-meter long train which moves at an average speed of 100 km/hr and crosses a platform in 27 seconds. A man crosses the same platform in 5 minutes. What is the speed of man in meter/second?
questions.solution_en:
Let the length of the platform be 'x' meters.

Speed of train = 100 km/hr = 100 * 5/18 = 250/9 meter/second

300 + x = (250/9) * 27

=> x = 750 - 300 = 450m

∴ Required speed of man = 450/(5 * 60) = 1.5 meter/second

questions.q_en: Two trains approach each other at (X - 3) kmph and (X + 3) kmph from 2 places, 1470 km apart. If they meet after 21 hours, then the value of X is:
questions.solution_en:

2X = 1470/21

2X = 70

X = 35

questions.q_en: A train crosses a 300 m tunnel in 60 s and passes a man running at 9 km/h in the opposite direction in 24 s. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.solution_en:
9 km/h = 2.5 m/s

Let, train speed be v m/s and length be L m.

When train crosses tunnel of 400 m ---

(L + 300)/60 = v

L = 60v - 300 ..... (1)

When train crosses man in opposite direction ---

L = 24(v + 2.5) ..... (2)

Solving (1) and (2), we get -

60v − 300 = 24v + 60

=> 36v = 360

=> v = 10 m/s = 36 km/h

questions.q_en: Two trains, one 150 m and the other 100 m long, are traveling towards each other on parallel tracks at speeds of 54 km/h and 36 km/h respectively. How many seconds will they take to completely pass each other?
questions.solution_en:
Length of Train A = 150 m

Length of Train B = 100 m

Total distance to clear = 150 + 100 = 250 m

Speed of Train A = 54 km/h = 54 X (5/18) = 15 m/s

Speed of Train B = 36 km/h = 36 X (5/18) = 10 m/s

Since they move in opposite directions, relative speed = 15 + 10 = 25 m/s

Time to pass = [Total distance] / [Relative speed] = 250 / 25 = 10 seconds

Thus, they take 10 seconds to pass each other completely.

questions.q_en: A freight train travels at 36 km/h. A passenger train, 30 km/h faster than the freight train, overtakes it and crosses completely in 18 seconds. If the length of the passenger train is 120 m, find the length of the freight train (in m).
questions.solution_en:
Let L = length of freight train in meters

Speed of freight train = 36 km/h = 36 X (5/18) = 10 m/s

Speed of passenger train = 36 + 30 = 66 km/h = 66 X (5/18) = 55/3 m/s

Relative speed (same direction) = (55/3) − 10 = 25/3 m/s

According to question,

(120 + L) / (25/3) = 18

=> (120 + L) = 18 X (25/3) = 150

=> L = 150 − 120 = 30

Thus, the length of the freight train is 30 m.

questions.q_en: Two trains A and train B running at 55 m/s and 73 m/s respectively. If length of train A and train B is 280m and 360 m respectively. Find the time taken by them to cross each other.
questions.solution_en:
Respective speed = 55 + 73 = 128 m/sec

Time taken by trains to cross each other = (280 + 360)/128 = 640/128

=> 5 sec
